summary.text: A 61-year-old hypertensive, diabetic and unvaccinated man had one episode of mild fever and dry cough on day 1 of illness and tested COVID RT PCR positive on Day 2 of fever. On Day 5 he developed abnormal behavior, irrelevant speech and gibberish, apathy and progressive drowsiness.

He was admitted to primary care on Day 9, where hyponatremia was found without COVID pneumonia or cytokine storm and was corrected as per protocol, but the behavioral abnormality did not improve as expected. He was referred for further evaluation on Day 15.

Examination showed low mood and transcortical sensory aphasia with alexia and agraphia. MRI showed T2-hyperintense left temporo-parietal and thalamic lesions with insular ribboning and diffusion restriction, and PET showed severe left-sided hypometabolism. EEG was normal. CSF showed detectable SARS-Cov-2 IgG and spike protein antibodies; CSF PCR for the virus and HSV and the antibody and paraneoplastic panels were negative.

He fulfilled criteria for possible autoimmune encephalitis and received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by intravenous immunoglobulin at 2 g/kg divided over 5 days. The patient is on an improving course, with marked improvement in language function at 3 months of follow-up.
